questions.q: By 1900, did most people live in towns or the countryside?
Describe the trend in the chart in one sentence.
questions.a: The population rose steadily, roughly doubling

questions.q: Core: Complete the 'Britain in 1800 and 1900' table (population, where people lived, travel, work, lighting), then write which change mattered most and why.
questions.a: An accurate table and a reasoned choice

questions.q: Extend: Suggest two reasons the population grew so fast.
questions.a: More food, better medicine later in the century, more jobs in towns

questions.q: Stretch: How can a census help a family historian?
questions.a: It lists names, ages, jobs and addresses every ten years

questions.q: Between 1841 and 1901 the population of England and Wales:
questions.a: C) About doubled. It grew from about 16 million to about 32.5 million.

questions.q: Big question: would someone from 1800 recognise 1900?
questions.a: Partly: they would know the land, but towns, railways and factories would be new
